Base-promoted regio- and diastereoselective
synthesis of tri- and tetra-substituted homoallenyl
phosphine oxides via alkynyl enones†
Shaochan Zhou,a Haotian Zou,a Xianqiang Huang,
 *a Jialin Qi
 *a and
Zhenghu Xu
 b,c
A novel base-promoted method for hydrophosphinylation of alkynyl enones with secondary phosphine
oxides has been developed. Using inexpensive and commercially available potassium carbonate, a variety
of functionalized tri-substituted allene products were synthesized with exclusive regio- and diastereo-
selectivity under mild conditions. Furthermore, a one-pot, two-step, three-component tandem hydro-
phosphinylation/Heck reaction e ﬃciently produced tetra-substituted homoallenyl phosphine oxides in
excellent yields, demonstrating a relatively broad substrate scope.
Introduction
Allenes and their derivatives represent a distinct class of
organic compounds that have garnered significant interest in
recent years. 1–4 In particular, tri- and tetra-substituted allene
compounds containing various functionalities (Scheme 1a) are
receiving increasing attention due to their presence in numer-
ous bioactive molecules. 5–8 As a result, several e ﬀective syn-
thetic methodologies for multi-substituted allenes have been
developed.9–16 Among these synthons, alkynyl enones are
readily accessible, versatile building blocks developed by
Larock,
17 Zhang,18–21 and others. 22–26 1,4-Addition to alkynyl
enones provides a novel and e ﬃcient strategy for accessing
functionalized allenes. 27–34 Xu et al. 32 established a copper-
catalyzed 1,4-protosilylation of α-alkynylenones to form func-
tionalized chiral homoallenylsilanes (Scheme 1b, left). Yang 31
achieved the synthesis of tri-substituted allenes through asym-
metric additions of oxazolones to enynones, facilitated by
chiral phosphoric acid (CPA) catalysis (Scheme 1b, right).
Despite these significant contributions, there appears to be no
reported instance of a 1,4-addition reaction utilizing alkynyl
enones with a phosphorus nucleophile to synthesize homoalle-
nyl phosphines.
On the other hand, organophosphorus motifs have been
extensively employed in the design of chiral ligands and cata-
lysts, as well as in medicinal and materials chemistry.
35–40
Hydrophosphinylation of unsaturated carbon –carbon bonds
have emerged as direct and e ﬃcient strategies for constructing
structures that incorporate both allenes and organopho-
sphorus groups.
41–56 Recently, He 47 reported the reactions of
α-hydroxyalkylphosphonates, acting as masked phosphonating

Additionally, Ding ’s group 48 developed a visible-light-induced
radical-polar crossover 1,4-hydrophosphinylation of 1,3-
enynes, enabling the formation of trisubstituted allenes featur-
ing a phosphine oxide group. Several previous studies have
attempted to establish diastereoselective processes related to
the synthesis of homoallenyl phosphines. However, they typi-
cally resulted in 1 : 1 diastereoselectivity for the
transformation.
Thus, we aim to accomplish regio- and diastereoselective
synthesis of multi-substituted homoallenyl phosphines. Given
the importance of multi-substituted allenes and organopho-
sphorus compounds, along with our focus on the transform-
ation of alkynyl enones,
22 we have designed a hydrophosphiny-
lation reaction using alkynyl enones and secondary phosphine
oxides to generate tri- and tetra-substituted homoallenyl phos-
phines(Scheme 1c).
Results and discussion
Alkynyl enone 1a and diphenylphosphine oxide 2a were
selected to evaluate the viability of this hypothesis without any
additives. In our preliminary test, the reaction successfully
occurred using DCM as the solvent at room temperature (entry
1, Table 1), and the desired tri-substituted homoallenyl phos-
phine oxide was isolated in 25% yield without diastereo-
selectivity (3a/3a′ = 50/50). Encouraged by this initial result, we
proceeded with screening various bases to improve both the
yield and diastereoselectivity of the reaction. Both organic and
inorganic bases were e ﬀective in facilitating the reaction, pro-
viding products in good to excellent yields (entries 2 –4). The
type and amount of base were found to significantly influence
diastereoselectivity. When 4 equivalents of K
2CO3 were used,
the product was isolated in 92% yield with the best diastereo-
selectivity (88/12 dr). Reducing the equivalents of base or 2a
resulted in diminished yield and diastereoselectivity (entries
5–7). Solvent screening revealed that DCM remained the best
solvent (entries 8 –10). When THF was used as the solvent,
another diastereomer, 3a′, emerged as the major product, but
the yield dropped sharply to 34% (entry 8). At present, we have
not achieved satisfactory results for the isomer 3a′ (for
additional optimization results, see the ESI †).
Following the establishment of optimised conditions, the
substrate scope of base-promoted hydrophosphinylation was
next investigated. As summarized in Table 2, the scope is quite
broad, with reactions requiring 26 hours and yielding the
corresponding tri-substituted homoallenyl phosphine oxides
in good to excellent yields with good diastereoselectivities.
First, the reactivities of various alkynyl enones were examined.
Diverse halogens, such as F, Cl, and Br, as well as electron-
donating groups like CH
3, OCH 3 and OTs were well tolerated
in this reaction. Substrates containing a 2-naphthyl group ( 3i)
and heterocycles such as thienyl ( 3f ) were also compatible with
the transformation, delivering corresponding allenes in 59%
and 52% yields respectively. When the substituent (R 2) on the
ketone moiety was replaced with a methyl-substituted ketone
(2l), the corresponding product 3l was obtained in an excellent
yield (94%) with 57/43 diastereoselectivity. Next, a series of
substituted diaryl phosphine oxides were studied to evaluate
the potential for synthetic elaboration under the optimal con-
ditions. Electron-donating substituents on the phenyl rings
were compatible, yielding products ( 3m–3o) with 84% –98%
yields and diastereomeric ratios of 56 : 44 to 78 : 22.

Subsequently, a novel one-pot, two-step, three-component
tandem hydrophosphinylation/Heck reaction was
developed.57–59 This reaction involves electron-deficient
enynes, secondary phosphine oxides, and aryl halides to
provide highly functionalized tetrasubstituted allenes
(Table 3). However, the complex reaction system, characterized
by numerous byproducts, an elusive reaction mechanism, and
poor reaction e ﬃciency, makes this process quite challenging.
The intermolecular nucleophile, diaryl phosphine oxides,
initially attacks to form an allenyl intermediate. Subsequently,
the potential reaction pathway depends on the Lewis acidity of
the ArPdX species generated by the oxidative addition of aryl
halides with a Pd(0) catalyst. By utilising Lewis acid catalysis,
several tetra-substituted homoallenyl phosphine oxides were
successfully synthesised.
Herein, we report the Heck reaction of allenes, produced by
hydrophosphinylation of alkynyl enones, carried out at 80 °C
catalysed by 5 mol% Pd(PPh
3)4 in the presence of K 2CO3 (4.0
equiv.) as a base (Table 3). The coupling reaction between 2a
and 4a is performed, 60–62 therefore a one-pot approach is
employed to progressively add reaction reagents, ensuring that
the cascade reaction proceeds in a controlled manner. After
careful optimization, reducing the loading of diphenyl-
phosphine oxide to 1.5 equiv. and raising the reaction temp-
erature to 90 °C, the desired tetrasubstituted allene 5a was iso-
lated in 80% yield. As illustrated in Table 4, a variety of structu-
rally interesting tetra-substituted homoallenyl phosphine
oxides were obtained in good yields, and the structure of 5c
was unambiguously confirmed by X-ray di ﬀraction analysis.
Tri-substituted homoallenyl phosphine oxides could readily
undergo various classical transformations to a ﬀord syntheti-
cally useful chiral building blocks and bioactive molecules
(Scheme 2a). The gold(
I)-catalyzed rearrangement of 3a pro-
duced the tri-substituted furan derivative 6 in 84% yield and
its structure was unambiguously confirmed by X-ray di ﬀraction
analysis ([eqn (1)], Scheme 2a). 63 Furthermore, when
treated with 1.2 equiv. of benzoyl hydrazine 7 at 60 °C, 3b was

transformed into the tetra-substituted 5-hydroxypyrazoline 8 in
78% yield with >20 : 1 dr ([eqn (2)], Scheme 2a). Notably, the
family of 8 has been reported to possess antimicrobial, 64 anti-
inflammatory,65 antimalarial,66 hypolipidemic,67 and analgesic
activities.68 To elucidate the mechanism and operative
pathway of the diastereoselective 1,4-hydrophosphinylation
reaction, we conducted mechanistic experiments. Monitoring
the reaction progress revealed that alkynyl enones 1a essen-
tially completed the hydrophosphinylation reaction in about
6 hours, giving only 50 : 50 diastereoselectivity. Subsequently,
with the aid of the base K
2CO3, the dr value gradually
increased, with the optimum result achieved at 26 hours
(Scheme 2b). After this point, the diastereoselectivity
decreased precipitously, so we controlled the reaction time of
alkynyl enones and diarylphosphineoxides to 26 h and tested
diastereoselective transformations of tri-substituted homoalle-
nyl phosphine oxide 3a in the presence of a base using a
single isomer (Scheme 2c). The decline in dr value of tri-substi-
tuted allenes over time serves as a significant indication of the
pivotal role that the base plays in the hydrophosphinylation.
Based on the experimental results outlined above, the pro-
posed mechanism is depicted in Scheme 3. Initially, R
2P(O)H
is deprotonated to form the phosphoryl anion A in the pres-
ence of a base. This anion then undergoes the 1,4-addition
reaction with the alkynyl enone, generating the allenyl carba-
nion intermediate B. Intermediate B can extract a proton (H
+)
from SPOs, leading to the formation of the tri-substituted
homoallenyl phosphine oxide 3 and the regeneration of the
phosphoryl anion A. The two-component product 3 can then
undergo the Heck reaction with an aryl iodide in the presence
of Pd(0). The resulting aryl palladium( II) intermediate C,
formed via the oxidative addition of iodobenzene, undergoes
the migratory insertion with compound 3, forming the allyl –
Pd complex D. Finally, the β-H elimination reaction occurs,
yielding the tetra-substituted homologous phosphine oxide 5
and product E.
Conclusions
In summary, we have successfully developed an e ﬃcient 1,4-
addition of alkynyl enones under mild conditions, providing
tri- and tetra-substituted homoallenyl phosphine oxides. Using
only the inexpensive potassium carbonate, various functiona-
lized tri-substituted allenes were generated in moderate to
excellent yields with complete regio- and diastereoselectivity. A
base-promoted and Pd(0)-catalyzed one-pot, two-step, three-
component tandem hydrophosphinylation/Heck reaction of
alkynyl enones, diarylphosphineoxides and aryl iodides
resulted in tetra-substituted allenes. These simple and
eﬃcient methods further expand the synthetic potential of
these scaﬀolds in organic synthesis.

synthesis of tri- and tetra-substituted homoallenyl

Introduction

A novel base-promoted method for hydrophosphinylation of alkynyl enones with secondary phosphine
oxides has been developed. Using inexpensive and commercially available potassium carbonate, a variety
of functionalized tri-substituted allene products were synthesized with exclusive regio- and diastereo-
selectivity under mild conditions. Furthermore, a one-pot, two-step, three-component tandem hydro-
phosphinylation/Heck reaction eficiently produced tetra-substituted homoallenyl phosphine oxides in
excellent yields, demonstrating a relatively broad substrate scope.

Based on the experimental results outlined above, the pro-
posed mechanism is depicted in Scheme 3. Initially, R<sub>2</sub>P(O)H
is deprotonated to form the phosphoryl anion A in the pres-
ence of a base. This anion then undergoes the 1,4-addition
reaction with the alkynyl enone, generating the allenyl carba-

the migratory insertion with compound 3, forming the allyl–

yielding the tetra-substituted homologous phosphine oxide 5
and product E.
Conclusions

In summary, we have successfully developed an eficient 1,4-
addition of alkynyl enones under mild conditions, providing

tri- and tetra-substituted homoallenyl phosphine oxides. Using
only the inexpensive potassium carbonate, various functiona-
lized tri-substituted allenes were generated in moderate to
excellent yields with complete regio- and diastereoselectivity. A
base-promoted and Pd(0)-catalyzed one-pot, two-step, three-
component tandem hydrophosphinylation/Heck reaction of
alkynyl enones, diarylphosphineoxides and aryl iodides
resulted in tetra-substituted allenes. These simple and
eficient methods further expand the synthetic potential of
these scafolds in organic synthesis.
